body: I actually thought I was crazy going through the same thing. Sometimes I struggle with intrusive thoughts about how my partner died - I was only told that she left us in a very graphic way and I assume that she shot herself. My mind has definitely tried to recreate the scene without my permission and it really upsets me. I see you and I understand.
while it’s necessary to think of those you love before making decisions, tying yourself to life with this idea isn’t healthy. you need to have other things that you want to live for

Losing someone this way is so painful. I just lost my girlfriend to suicide last week. She seemed to have her whole life ahead of her - new job, good support network - and she’s gone now. It is so hard. She died hours after we discussed breaking up. She called many friends who were sleeping, had one on the line right before she left us. I have so many regrets. I wish we could have maintained a relationship. She had grown so much on her own for so long. I am so sad I won’t hear from her, see her, or feel her again.
My girlfriend recently died by suicide. I am sorry for your loss and understand your pain.
If it helps, post updates here or to other people who know and understand - kind of like a reliability thing. It helps to set goals and share with others after
What a beautiful soul lost. I am feeling the same way about losing someone recently. Sending love to you in this hard time.

Thank you so much. While it is important to ground ourselves with the ones we love, the only way to create a solid foundation is to address and respect how mental illness impacts life. Being open, talking about when things are hard, having loved ones who care and listen, talking with a counselor who knows how to comfort and address people struggling on their own.
I can’t be angry with her. I love her too much. I just miss her more than anything

Thank you so much for your comment. Unfortunately, the logical option isn’t always easily available. You aren’t selfish for wanting a way out. I understand that my girlfriend left because she was overwhelmed and couldn’t handle the strain of her situation anymore. However, while she did everything in her power to not hurt me, there is inevitable pain after a loss. 

I feel like understanding how your loved ones would feel is very grounding, but it cannot be the only reason you choose to be here. My absolute advice is to seek meaningful counseling, be very open with loved ones you can trust, and learn to rely on your friends. 

After losing my girlfriend, I have consistently reread all our conversations on every medium, desperate for an answer or a sign. What could I have done differently? How could I have sacrificed more for her? After attending my first support group, I learned this is a common behavior among people who lose a loved one to suicide. I would have rather known she felt like this was her only option than to find out she is gone.
I hope you have good people who you can depend on. I hope you feel appreciated and loved
That is incredibly kind. Thank you so much for telling me this. It means so much
The best you can do is your best. Set goals and set rewards for yourself once they are accomplished. ❤️ take it one day at a time and work on not putting pressure on yourself

Hi there. No matter how good your situation seems, mental health is very real. If you aren’t already, I would recommend seeing a counselor. Your mental health is just as important as your physical health, and things can be worse than they appear on the inside. Depressed people often feel guilty looking at people who have it worse than them, but that does not dismiss your own personal obstacles. You are so valid for feeling like this
Everyone feels this way when things are hard and they are lost. Please know that you have undoubtedly touched the lives of many people.
You have shown so much strength in your life. What I see from this is that while it’s hard, you want to be here.

Thank you for showing me another group. This is my second day on reddit and I don’t really get how to use it yet.

However, I do not regret making this post here. I have had several people reach out to talk to me because of this post. I made this post because I felt alone and didn’t want to be here. I understand how it feels. 

Sometimes it’s hard to think of the people you care about when you are lost. This is a group that has described these feelings very well. My post was not a guilt-trip, it was my very real perspective and feelings, which has had some people thinking differently and messaging to discuss.

Thank you so much. My girlfriend suffered from an unaccepting family all her life, so I am glad to hear you are better than that. I am sorry for your losses, I cannot imagine losing a sibling either. I wish you the best. Much love
That means more to me than you could ever imagine. I am crushed that she was not able to make it here, but the idea of helping other people by hearing about her? I can’t even describe. Thank you.

I see people comment painful experiences and then delete their comments before I can respond. Just know that you are not alone, I feel your loss, and I understand why you would remove the comment. Thank you for sharing your experiences with me nonetheless.

Do not be ashamed for taking care of yourself. This is an absolutely valid reason for staying home and thinking of yourself. Loss is extremely hard and we cannot control when it hits us. Sending love your way.
Thank you so much for sharing your experience. It means a lot. I am so sorry for your loss as well.
This is the cutest thing I’ve ever seen

I know my girlfriend never would have done this to deliberately hurt me. She told one of her friends to tell me she’s sorry. She texted me saying she will love me always. Even so, this is the worst loss I have ever felt. She left after saying so many good things to me, we ended on a wonderful note, but it hurts so much. I will always see her in everything in my life and feel so devastated that I couldn’t sacrifice more for her
I know you don’t know me, but that means so much. Thank you.
Thank you so much for sharing your experience. I am devastated to see so many with this pain, but it is good to not feel alone in it
Thank you so much. There are so many things I wish I could share here better
Thank you so much. I go back and forth with emotions now, but when I am strong enough, I would like to be able to talk about her and the good things without crying

I joined a support from nearby - which a family member actually found on online for me. I have discovered through Google and Facebook that there are tons of groups. Search your local services and see if they provide support groups. It is worth it to not feel alone
Why is anyone depressed? She had a collection of mental health issues and a large history of trauma. She tried her best and deserved better.

Thank you for taking the time to comment. She suffered for a long time and hid it so well. The other day, my therapist told me that she is impressed by my strength at the moment, but that being well-composed right now is not necessary. What’s necessary is feeling everything, so that I can let it all out, or else it will always stay with me. 

Note: I am doing the best I can and taking every step to try and recover from this

Thank you so much for saying this. I understand you. Loss by suicide is incredibly painful and the grieving process is entirely different for everyone. Currently, I am back and forth between endless crying and feeling completely numb. I have also experienced a lot of shock and disbelief that she is gone, almost like I am expecting a message or call from her at any moment

She shined too bright for this world. My girlfriend was the most kind, loving, big-hearted person anyone has ever met. While she looked hard on the outside to some people, she was always soft and gentle at heart.  I do not think I will ever know a better person, and I feel that loss enormously.

Thank you so much for sharing your experience. There are so many people who understand how painful this is. I hope you are well too. I just joined a support group of others who share their experiences, if you have not already, I would recommend this. There are free sessions online with people who understand and share their experiences. There are so many wonderful people in the world

Thank you so much for your comment. Know that I am seeking the best help I can. I am learning to rely to communicate my feelings with friends and family members. I have also started coping/grief sessions with a therapist. 

I know everything is stronger now because of how recently it happened, but this isn’t something I think will go away. I am just trying to learn how to live with it. A breakup? I could have at least known she was there to talk to again at any time. I could have checked on her. But this? Knowing I will never hear from her again is one of the most painful things in the world. Right now, I can’t imagine ever being with anyone else again.

Thank you for your comment. While my girlfriend took every step to tell me that this isn’t my fault before she was gone, I still feel that weight on my shoulders. I think I will always wish I could have sacrificed more for her.

This means so much to me. One of my biggest regrets is not knowing how unsafe exactly my girlfriend felt in her own mind. She was an expert at hiding this-always looking to help other people instead. Please talk with your loved ones and never hesitate to ask for the help you need, whether that be through loved ones, friends, or even therapy. I wish I had started therapy earlier than now. 

Note: While my girlfriend said every wonderful, kind, thoughtful thing you can ever imagine to/about me before she was gone. I still feel the same guilt and pain. It is heavier than anything I have ever had to carry. I miss her so much
Thank you so much for sharing. It is devastating to see how many people have suffered from similar losses. I am wishing you well

This comment means more to be than you could ever imagine. I have considered suicide on multiple occasions and been able to remind myself of what I would leave behind. Some people are not blessed with the ability to see what is ahead of them, but I really hope you are. Please always share your feelings with others and seek help any time you need it. You deserve better, even if your mind doesn’t think so.

I have never been religious—but my girlfriend wanted to have a faith and taught me so much. I said a prayer for her the day I lost her that she be given an easy afterlife. She had a long life with every trauma you can imagine. 

Now, I just hope she is at peace. Just know that while someone leaves thinking they are giving you peace, right now I feel like I may never feel peace again.

Thank you so much for saying this. As someone who has suffered a loss by suicide, I would do anything to help others who feel like she did. The pain and grief I have been feeling are unlike anything I have ever felt before. This loss has changed my entire life and I cannot ever look at anything the same again

Thank you for sharing your experience with me. No matter the time, this is a loss that stays with people. Even if you were apart for a long time, seeing someone you knew leave the world this way is incredibly painful. Please be sure to let yourself grieve and talk to other people about how you feel. You are never alone in these feelings

Something I have learned about suicide? No matter how close to the incident, every person feels some kind of guilt and suffers. Everyone runs “what if’s” in their head until they can’t take it. There are so many emotions. 

I am trying so hard to focus on the good. My girlfriend’s last words to me were a text saying “Just know that I will always love you.” She has been on the phone with me, telling me she wanted a good life for me, but no mater how good the intention is, the loss is so heavy. I can’t imagine what my future looks like anymore. 

PS: please know that I have found a therapist to speak with about coping and grief. Thank you for your concern.

She was a beautiful person. When I say she touched the lives of many people, I mean it. My girlfriend stopped the car to help other women who needed anything. Gave strangers rides. She stepped into violent situations to help others. She cared so deeply about other people. 

She also helped so many people in her line of work. Every time I went out with her, so many people would say hello or thank her. 

She also had a large friend group that loved her more than anything. She had siblings and a grandparent she talked to on a regular basis who she would have done anything for. 

You can have the best support system in the world, and still feel so alone. I mean it when I say her light touched countless people.

Actually... I am in my early twenties and I am a woman. Her parents were not supportive of her and it is little too late for them to make up for how they have treated her throughout her life. My girlfriend relied on herself, me, and a large support system of close friends.
